# How much of the temperature–ozone effect is real?

`datasets::airquality`, 153 rows. Ozone is missing in 37 rows and Solar.R in 7, so
111 rows have every variable. All numbers below come from run
`airquality-temp-5` (`analysis.R`, digest `1f6dd06c…`) and from
`artifact.check` on that run, which reported `integrity: verified` for four files.

## Models

| model | specification | n | temp effect (ppb/°F) | 95% CI | share of A |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Ozone ~ Temp | 116 | 2.429 | 1.967 – 2.891 | 1.000 |
| B | Ozone ~ Temp + Wind | 116 | 1.840 | 1.345 – 2.335 | 0.758 |
| C | Ozone ~ Temp + Wind, complete rows only | 111 | 1.828 | 1.331 – 2.324 | 0.752 |
| D | Ozone ~ Temp + Wind + Solar.R | 111 | 1.652 | 1.150 – 2.155 | 0.680 |

## Decomposition of the 32% drop

- **Wind adjustment: −24.2 points** (A → B). This is the real confounder:
  adding one variable removes a quarter of the raw temperature effect, and the
  nested F test says the added term earns its place (F = 21.2, p = 1.1e−05).
- **Sample restriction: −0.5 points** (B → C). Dropping the five rows that lack
  Solar.R changes almost nothing, so the missingness is not driving the story.
- **Solar radiation: −7.2 points** (C → D). Smaller, but not noise: F = 6.66,
  p = 0.011.

So the honest sentence is: **temperature still matters after adjustment — about
two-thirds of the raw slope survives — but a third of the raw slope was wind and
sunlight, and wind is by far the larger share.** The raw 2.43 ppb/°F figure is not
a causal effect of temperature.

## What this run does not say

- No causality, no time structure: these are daily measurements with a strong
  seasonal correlation between temperature and solar radiation.
- The 37 missing ozone rows are assumed missing at random; nothing here tests that.
- One dataset, one specification family. Ozone ~ Temp + Wind + Solar.R + Month
  would be the next thing to try.

# Question: how much of the temperature effect on ozone survives adjustment for
# wind and solar radiation, and how much of the change is just a change of sample?
# Every number below comes from this run; nothing is typed in from elsewhere.
out <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)[1]

data(airquality, package = "datasets")
d <- datasets::airquality
vars <- c("Ozone", "Solar.R", "Wind", "Temp")
miss <- vapply(vars, function(v) sum(is.na(d[[v]])), integer(1))

# ozone-core drops only rows without ozone/wind/temp; complete also drops solar.
core <- d[complete.cases(d[, c("Ozone", "Wind", "Temp")]), ]
cc   <- d[complete.cases(d[, vars]), ]

tidy <- function(label, sample, m) {
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients
  data.frame(model = label, sample = sample, n = nobs(m), term = rownames(co),
             estimate = co[, "Estimate"], std.error = co[, "Std. Error"],
             statistic = co[, "t value"], p.value = co[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
             r2 = summary(m)$r.squared, adj.r2 = summary(m)$adj.r.squared,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}

m0 <- lm(Ozone ~ Temp, core)                        # A: raw, ozone-core
m1 <- lm(Ozone ~ Temp + Wind, core)                 # B: wind, same rows
m2 <- lm(Ozone ~ Temp + Wind, cc)                   # C: wind, complete rows
m3 <- lm(Ozone ~ Temp + Wind + Solar.R, cc)         # D: + solar, complete rows
coefs <- rbind(tidy("A", "ozone-core", m0), tidy("B", "ozone-core", m1),
               tidy("C", "complete", m2), tidy("D", "complete", m3))
write.csv(coefs, file.path(out, "coefficients.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

temp_row <- function(label, sample, m) {
  est <- unname(coef(m)["Temp"]); se <- unname(sqrt(vcov(m)["Temp", "Temp"]))
  tc <- qt(0.975, df.residual(m))
  data.frame(model = label, sample = sample, n = nobs(m), estimate = est,
             std.error = se, ci.low = est - tc * se, ci.high = est + tc * se,
             p.value = unname(summary(m)$coefficients["Temp", "Pr(>|t|)"]))
}
effects <- rbind(temp_row("A", "ozone-core", m0), temp_row("B", "ozone-core", m1),
                 temp_row("C", "complete", m2), temp_row("D", "complete", m3))
base <- effects$estimate[1]
effects$share.of.A <- effects$estimate / base
effects$change.vs.previous <- c(NA, diff(effects$estimate) / base)
write.csv(effects, file.path(out, "effects.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

a01 <- anova(m0, m1); a23 <- anova(m2, m3)
tests <- data.frame(test = c("wind added (B vs A)", "solar added (D vs C)"),
                    df = c(a01$Df[2], a23$Df[2]),
                    f = c(a01$F[2], a23$F[2]),
                    p.value = c(a01$`Pr(>F)`[2], a23$`Pr(>F)`[2]))
write.csv(tests, file.path(out, "tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

png(file.path(out, "temp-effect.png"), width = 1040, height = 620, res = 110)
op <- par(mar = c(4.6, 8.2, 4, 2))
plot(NA, xlim = range(c(effects$ci.low, effects$ci.high)), ylim = c(0.4, nrow(effects) + 0.6),
     yaxt = "n", xlab = "Ozone change per 1 F temperature (ppb, 95% CI)", ylab = "",
     main = "Temperature effect under four specifications")
abline(h = seq_len(nrow(effects)), col = "grey92"); abline(v = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey45")
segments(effects$ci.low, seq_len(nrow(effects)), effects$ci.high, seq_len(nrow(effects)), lwd = 2.2)
points(effects$estimate, seq_len(nrow(effects)), pch = 19, cex = 1.5)
axis(2, at = seq_len(nrow(effects)), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.85,
     labels = sprintf("%s  n=%d  %s", effects$model, effects$n, effects$sample))
text(effects$estimate, seq_len(nrow(effects)) + 0.24, sprintf("%.3f", effects$estimate), cex = 0.72)
par(op); invisible(dev.off())

files <- c("coefficients.csv", "effects.csv", "tests.csv", "temp-effect.png")
artifacts <- lapply(files, function(f) {
  p <- file.path(out, f)
  list(path = f, bytes = unname(file.size(p)),
       sha256 = digest::digest(p, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE))
})
manifest <- list(schemaVersion = 1L, complete = TRUE, artifacts = artifacts)
writeLines(jsonlite::toJSON(manifest, auto_unbox = TRUE), file.path(dirname(out), "inventory.json"))

cat("n rows:", nrow(d), " missing:", paste(names(miss), miss, sep = "=", collapse = " "), "\n")
cat("temp coefficient by model (ppb per F):\n"); print(effects[, c("model", "n", "estimate", "ci.low", "ci.high")], row.names = FALSE)
cat("share of raw estimate kept:", paste(sprintf("%.3f", effects$share.of.A), collapse = " "), "\n")
